verdict.rationale: mise installs prebuilt binaries rather than building from source through several backends. It can install ripgrep "directly from GitHub releases" ([mise-docs-54], [mise-docs-4]), and the github/aqua backends reach "almost all programs available on GitHub" ([mise-docs-57]). It also accepts per-platform prebuilt tarball URLs with checksums ([mise-docs-26]), and a user confirms it replaced their manual binary-download workflows ([mise-comm-14]). However, nothing describes a binary cache, or prebuilt builds of runtimes like Python/Ruby that would otherwise be compiled. missing for 10: an explicit prebuilt/precompiled binary cache, documentation that language runtimes install from prebuilt artifacts instead of compiling, any comparison of install speed versus source builds.
